38.subject: Re: Problems with home directory install
38.message_body:
Just one thing that it appears that everyone knows but that can't
be stressed enough.

Many of us only have ftp and web access to our sites.

So we can hack config files at home and upload to the site
but we can't run any scripts, except via the web on the site.

And quite often it's hard to convince the host admins to hack
http.conf or php.ini on request.

So please please, don't forget us poor bastards who have to live
with what we have.

 <gmane_tag_closing> ps.
I have to admit that I actually can, since I have a local install
at home on my own server and uses weex to update the main site.
But the problems are common.
ds.

58.subject: Remote security
58.message_body:
The machine I use day to day is the machine I sure as the server for unison.

I have a laptop that syncs with it
A linux media centre (MythTV) that I plan to sync with it as soon as I 
get the right unison version on there
and a machine in an office in London that I only go to once per month or so.

Currently, to sync the London machine, I log into it using TightVNC over 
Hamachi (can't get ssh to work in the direction from my home machine to 
the office so I use hamachi) then run unison from there.

Before yesterday, I would manually run Putty every time I wanted to 
sync, which was a pain, but as least meant that an ssh connection from 
the office machine to my machine was only temporary.

Now, I've set up Pageant so that I don't have to use putty all the time 
(although that's not cured a problem I was having so not sure how great 
a solution it is) which is handy. The down side is that I'm feeling 
insecure about a constant ssh tunnel from a location I can't monitor to 
my main machine.

Is there anything I can do to make this more secure?
Can I somehow make unison the only app that it's possible to run over 
ssh/pageant?

I can't even think of other possibilities, but looking forward to 
hearing any thoughts.

 <gmane_tag_closing> <gmane_tag_mua_signature>

67.subject: sqlcounter problem after upgrading to 2.1.0
67.message_body:
<gmane_tag_salutation> I've been using freeradius 1.1.5 for sometime. I use mysql for storing users
and I have enabled sqlcounter module for restricitng monthly access time.
Each user is member of a group and group's Max-Monthly-Session is set in
radgroupcheck table. I have a script which is invoked from cron every month
which calculates remaining time of users and does a insert/update/delete on
radcheck so that there will be a record in radcheck if the user has any time
left from the prevois month. Attribute is Max-Monthly-Session and value =
(remaining + group's Max-Monthly-Session). This way I have implemented a
session time carry over system.

Recently I have upgraded freeradius to version 2.1.0. Everything is working
well as expected other than sqlcounter. In new version it is ignoring the
Max-Monthly-Session from radcheck table. I have installed radius in a new
server but the same result. The radius debug output and sql table are
available at http://pastebin.ca/1204050

Is there any config item for sqlcounter to process radcheck table?

 <gmane_tag_closing> <gmane_tag_visual_separator> <gmane_tag_mua_signature>
